background_notes.fact: A finite extended diameter d equals ofReal(d.toReal); finite extended-diameter inequalities transfer to the corresponding nonnegative real diameters. If a nonempty B⊆ℝ satisfies |b−b'|≤r for every b,b'∈B, where r≥0 is finite, then B is bounded, inf B≤b≤sup B for b∈B, and sup B−inf B≤r.

background_notes.justification: Finite extended nonnegative reals are order-isomorphic to nonnegative real numbers, so toReal is legitimate under these bounds. Choosing b₀∈B gives B⊆[b₀−r,b₀+r]. Completeness of ℝ then gives its infimum and supremum. For fixed b'∈B, b≤b'+r for all b∈B, hence sup B≤b'+r. Thus sup B−r is a lower bound for B and is ≤inf B, proving the claimed length bound.

background_notes.fact: For real s>0, the function x↦x^s on [0,∞) is finite, nonnegative and increasing, with 0^s=0. For every finite x≥0, x^(s+1)=x^s x, including x=0. Consequently 1+x^s>0 and x^s/(1+x^s)≤1.

background_notes.justification: For x>0 these are the usual real-power laws from x^s=exp(s log x), monotonicity of log and exp and positivity of s. At x=0, positivity of both exponents s and s+1 gives zero and verifies the product identity. The ratio estimate follows by dividing x^s≤1+x^s by the positive denominator. These facts also justify the earlier slice-cost comparison and positivity of η_i.

background_notes.fact: Open intervals, closed intervals and ∅ are Borel subsets of ℝ; finite intersections of Borel sets are Borel. For a Borel set B and fixed w∈[0,∞], the function equal to w on B and 0 outside B is Borel measurable, and hence is almost-everywhere measurable for any measure on this measurable space.

The preimage of an open subset of the extended nonnegative reals under a two-valued indicator function is one of ∅, B, Bᶜ or ℝ, each measurable. A measurable representative is automatically an almost-everywhere measurable representative.
